metadata.title: Reinforcing or Balancing?
metadata.description: Six illustrative causal loops, two from Paul's world and four from school change, shown one at a time. Count the minus signs around each loop: even (including zero) is reinforcing, odd is balancing. Each loop is drawn around the origin; the sim shows one loop at a time.
metadata.author: Mediterranean Travels

nodes.label: Student results
nodes.description: How well students learn with the new method, for example the share of questions answered correctly.

nodes.label: Teacher confidence
nodes.description: How sure teachers feel that they can use the new method well.

nodes.label: Quality of use
nodes.description: How skillfully teachers use the new method in class.

nodes.label: Rollout speed
nodes.description: How fast the new method is pushed into classrooms.

nodes.label: Teacher overload
nodes.description: How much new work teachers carry at once.

nodes.label: Resistance
nodes.description: How much teachers push back against the change.

nodes.label: New initiatives launched
nodes.description: How many new programs leaders start in a year.

nodes.label: Change fatigue
nodes.description: Weariness and cynicism after one change follows another.

nodes.label: Effort on each initiative
nodes.description: How much time and care teachers give each program.

nodes.label: Student results
nodes.description: How well students learn.

nodes.label: Converts to Paul's message
nodes.description: How many people in Ephesus join the new movement.

nodes.label: Sales of silver shrines
nodes.description: How many silver shrines of Artemis the silversmiths sell (Acts 19:24).

nodes.label: Silversmiths' opposition
nodes.description: How strongly Demetrius and the silversmiths oppose Paul, up to the riot in the theater.

nodes.label: Honor given to weaker members
nodes.description: How much the community honors the members who seem weaker or less important (1 Corinthians 12:22-24).

nodes.label: Sense of belonging
nodes.description: How fully every member feels part of the body.

nodes.label: Members' care for one another
nodes.description: How much members look after each other: "if one member suffers, all suffer together with it."

nodes.label: Pressure for quick results
nodes.description: How hard leaders and the public push for results in the first months.

nodes.label: Teachers' fear of mistakes
nodes.description: How afraid teachers are of being seen to fail with the new method.

nodes.label: Practice with the new method
nodes.description: How much teachers actually use and practice the new method.

nodes.label: Student results
nodes.description: How well students learn.

edges.description: A faster rollout means more work.
More fatigue, less effort on each.
Care gives honor to the weak.

loops.label: Loop 1: Success in the rollout
loops.description: Zero minus signs is even: success feeds itself.
loops.behavior_pattern: Success compounds; so does failure, if results start to fall.

loops.label: Loop 2: Pushback against a fast rollout
loops.description: One minus sign is odd: pushing faster raises resistance that slows the rollout.
loops.behavior_pattern: The harder the push, the stronger the pushback; the rollout settles at the speed teachers can carry.

loops.label: Loop 3: One initiative after another
loops.description: Two minus signs is even: weak results prompt more initiatives, which deepen fatigue and weaken results further.
loops.behavior_pattern: A vicious circle: every new fix makes the next one more likely.

loops.label: Loop 4: The silversmiths push back
loops.description: Three minus signs is odd: growth of the movement provokes opposition that holds it back.
loops.behavior_pattern: The movement grows until the people who lose by it push back. Pliny's letter of about 112 CE reports the same pattern in Bithynia.

loops.label: Loop 5: One body, many parts
loops.description: Zero minus signs is even: Paul's body picture describes care that grows on itself.
loops.behavior_pattern: A virtuous circle: care and belonging build on each other.

loops.label: Loop 6: Pressure during the implementation dip
loops.description: Two minus signs is even: during an implementation dip, pressure causes fear, fear cuts practice, and lower results bring more pressure.
loops.behavior_pattern: Judging a change too early deepens the dip it is reacting to.
